title: Engine idles high
h1: Why is my engine idling high or revving on its own?
metaDesc: Engine idling high or revving by itself? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's normal, a vacuum leak, a sensor or a sticking throttle, and how urgent it is.
intro: A higher idle for a minute or two after a cold start is normal. An idle that stays high when warm, rises and falls on its own, or a car that pushes forward when you lift off the gas is not. Answer a few questions to find the likely cause and how soon to deal with it.
safety: If the car keeps speeding up on its own, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and steer to a safe place before turning the engine off.
If the gas pedal sticks or a floor mat is catching it, don't drive until it's fixed.
If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine shakes, pull over safely and turn it off.

q_what_happens.q: Which best describes what the engine is doing?
q_what_happens.help: Idle speed is shown on the tachometer (the RPM gauge). A warm engine usually idles somewhere under 1,000 RPM, but it varies by car.

opts.a: The car keeps speeding up when I lift off the gas, or the gas pedal sticks or comes up slowly
It idles high only for the first minute or two after a cold start, then settles down
It stays high even after the engine is fully warmed up
The RPM needle rises and falls by itself while stopped (hunting or surging)

q_warm_clues.help: These clues separate a leak, a sensor problem and a car that simply needs to relearn its idle.

opts.a: It started right after the battery was disconnected or replaced, or the throttle was cleaned
I hear a hiss or whistle from under the hood, or the check engine light is on
The temperature gauge stays low or the heater is weak
The idle also goes up and down by itself
None of these / I'm not sure

result.title: The throttle or gas pedal may be sticking open
result.now: Don't drive it. With the engine off, check that the floor mat isn't pushing on or catching the gas pedal. If the mat isn't the cause, have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If the car speeds up on its own while you're driving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and steer to a safe place, then turn the engine off.
If a loose or extra floor mat was trapping the pedal, remove it, secure the correct mat with its clips, and check that the pedal now springs back fully before using the car.
result.why: An engine that keeps revving when you lift your foot means the throttle isn't closing. That can make the car hard to slow down or stop, so it's a safety problem, not just an annoyance.

causes.name: Floor mat pushing on or trapping the gas pedal
causes.clues: An extra mat stacked on top of another, a mat that slides forward, or a pedal that frees up when you move the mat.
causes.against: If the pedal sticks with the mat removed, look elsewhere.

causes.name: Sticking gas pedal or throttle body
causes.clues: The pedal feels gritty or slow to return, or the problem is worse in cold or damp weather.

causes.name: Electronic throttle or pedal sensor fault
causes.clues: A check engine light or a reduced power message along with the revving.

you: With the engine off, press the gas pedal and let go. It should snap back smoothly.
Make sure there's only one floor mat on the driver's side and it's held by its clips.
Check for open recalls on your vehicle using your VIN.
shop: Code scan and live pedal and throttle position data

result.title: This sounds like the normal fast idle of a cold engine
result.now: If the idle drops back to normal within a few minutes, there's usually nothing to repair. Keep an eye on it.
if: If the idle stays high after the temperature gauge reaches its normal spot, have it checked.
If the idle is only a little higher with the A/C or defroster on, that's normal too. The engine raises it to carry the extra load.
If the car pushes forward when you lift off the gas, or the gas pedal sticks or comes up slowly, don't drive it until it's checked.
result.why: A cold engine runs a higher idle on purpose. It helps the engine run smoothly and warms up the parts that clean the exhaust faster. Once warm, the computer brings the idle back down.

causes.name: Normal cold-start fast idle
causes.clues: Higher RPM for a minute or two after starting, especially on cold mornings, then it settles.
causes.against: If it never settles, something else is going on.

causes.name: Normal idle boost from A/C or electrical load
causes.clues: The idle rises slightly when you turn on the A/C, defroster or headlights.

you: Watch the tachometer as the engine warms up and note how long the high idle lasts.
Compare idle with the A/C on and off.
shop: Code scan and idle speed check if it doesn't settle

result.title: The engine computer may need to relearn its idle
result.now: Let the engine idle in Park until it's fully warm with everything switched off, then drive normally for a few days. Many cars relearn the idle on their own.
if: If the idle is still high after a few days of normal driving, a shop can run the idle relearn procedure for your vehicle.
If the high idle comes with a check engine light, get the code read.
If the car pushes forward when you lift off the gas or is hard to slow down, stop driving it and have it checked.
result.why: Disconnecting the battery or cleaning the throttle can erase what the engine computer learned about holding a steady idle. Until it relearns, the idle can sit high or wander.

causes.name: Lost idle settings after a battery disconnect
causes.clues: The problem started right after a battery change, jump start or disconnect.

causes.name: Throttle cleaned without a relearn
causes.clues: It started right after the throttle body was cleaned.

you: Check your owner's manual for an idle relearn step after battery disconnection.
Note whether the idle improves over a few drives.
shop: Idle relearn procedure with a scan tool

result.title: Extra air leaking into the engine is a possible cause (vacuum leak)
result.now: Have the check engine code read, then book a vacuum leak test when convenient.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing or the engine runs very rough, stop driving and have it checked.
If you find a hose that has popped off, a shop can usually fix it quickly.
If the brake pedal feels hard or needs more force than usual, a brake booster hose may be leaking. Have it checked before driving further.
If the car pushes forward when you lift off the gas, stop driving it and have it towed.
result.why: The engine sets idle by controlling how much air gets in. A cracked hose or leaking gasket lets in extra air the computer can't control, so the idle rises. A hiss is often the leak itself. A shop will usually smoke-test the intake to find the leak before replacing parts.

causes.name: Cracked, split or disconnected vacuum hose
causes.clues: A hiss or whistle at idle, or an older car with brittle rubber hoses.

causes.name: Leaking intake gasket or air intake boot
causes.clues: A lean-mixture check engine code, or a rough idle along with the high idle.

causes.name: Leaking brake booster hose or PCV valve
causes.clues: The idle changes when you press the brake pedal.

you: With the engine idling, listen around the top of the engine for a hiss. Keep hands away from belts and the fan.
Have the check engine code read. Many auto parts stores offer this.
shop: Code scan and fuel trim data

result.title: The engine may think it's still cold
result.now: Book a check when convenient. Mention that the temperature gauge stays low or the heater is weak.
if: If the temperature gauge ever climbs into the red, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the check engine light is on, get the code read. It can point toward the sensor or thermostat circuit, and a shop will usually confirm with live data before replacing parts.
If the coolant is low, have the cooling system checked for a leak soon. Low coolant can lead to overheating.
result.why: The computer keeps a fast idle until it sees the engine is warm. A thermostat stuck open keeps the engine from warming up, and a faulty temperature sensor can report cold when it isn't. Either way the idle stays high.

causes.name: Thermostat stuck open
causes.clues: The temperature gauge stays low on the highway, and the heater is lukewarm.
causes.against: If the gauge reads normal and the heater is hot, the thermostat is probably fine.

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature sensor
causes.clues: A check engine light, worse fuel economy, or a gauge that reads oddly.

causes.name: Low coolant
causes.clues: The coolant reservoir is below the MIN line.

you: With the engine cold, check the coolant reservoir level.
Note where the temperature gauge sits after 15 minutes of driving.
shop: Code scan and live coolant temperature data

result.title: The idle control system may be dirty or faulty
result.now: Book a check when convenient. Note whether the surging happens warm or cold, and with the A/C on or off.
if: If the engine stalls when you slow down or come to a stop, avoid driving it until it's checked. When the engine dies, steering and braking take much more effort.
If you also hear a hiss, a vacuum leak is the more likely cause.
If the car pushes forward when you lift off the gas, stop driving it and have it towed.
result.why: The engine uses a throttle valve or a small idle air valve to hold a steady idle. When carbon builds up or a part starts failing, the computer keeps overcorrecting and the RPM hunts up and down.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body
causes.clues: Black buildup around the throttle plate, and an idle that has slowly gotten worse.

causes.name: Faulty idle air control valve (older cars)
causes.clues: The surging comes and goes, and may be worse when cold.
causes.against: Many newer cars have no separate idle valve.

causes.name: Small vacuum leak
causes.clues: A faint hiss, or a check engine code for a lean mixture.

you: Watch the tachometer at idle and note how far it swings.
Have the check engine code read if the light is on.

result.title: A high idle that won't settle needs a quick check
result.now: Have the check engine code read if the light is on, and book an inspection when convenient.
if: If the car pushes forward when you lift off the gas, or the pedal sticks, stop driving it and have it towed.
If the temperature gauge stays low, mention it. It can point to a thermostat or sensor.
If the check engine light flashes or the engine shakes, pull over safely and turn it off.
result.why: A high idle usually comes from extra air getting in, a sensor telling the computer the engine is cold, or an idle control part that isn't working. A technician can tell which with a scan tool and a smoke test.

causes.name: Temperature sensor or thermostat
causes.clues: A low temperature gauge or weak heat.

causes.name: Dirty or faulty throttle body
causes.clues: The idle goes up and down.

you: Note the RPM at idle once warm, with the A/C off.
Record a short video of the tachometer at idle for the shop.
